name: Knee bounce
summary: Soft knees that dip a little on each beat. Almost every other move sits on top of this.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft
On each beat, let your knees dip a few centimetres
Come back up between beats, but never lock your knees
Let your shoulders and head ride along with the bounce
tips: Find the kick drum first and bounce only on that
Smaller is cooler: a tiny bounce on time beats a big one off time
mistakes: Bouncing up on the beat instead of down
Locking the knees between bounces, which makes it look stiff
why: Feeling the beat in your knees is what makes the rest of your body look like it's dancing to the music rather than next to it.

name: Step-touch
summary: Step to one side, bring the other foot in to tap, then go back the other way.
steps: Step your right foot out to the right (1)
Bring your left foot in and tap it next to the right (2)
Step your left foot out to the left (3)
Tap the right foot next to it (4)
tips: Keep the knee bounce going underneath
Once it's automatic, let your shoulders swing the opposite way to your feet
mistakes: Stepping too wide, which eats floor space and pulls you off the beat

name: Weight-shift sway
summary: Feet stay put while your weight rolls from one foot to the other, and the hips follow.
steps: Feet a bit wider than hip-width, knees soft
Shift your weight over the left foot on 1, so the right heel can lift
Shift over the right foot on 2
Let the hips and shoulders follow the weight, not lead it
tips: Try it at half speed (one shift every two beats) for slow tracks
This is the move to fall back on when you've lost the beat
mistakes: Swinging only the hips while the weight stays in the middle

name: Loose arms
summary: Give your hands somewhere to be: elbows bent, hands around waist to chest height, moving with the body.
steps: Bend your elbows and bring your hands up to between waist and chest
Loosen your fists, or make them soft
Let the hands rise and fall a little with the knee bounce
Every few bars, change it: one arm swings, or both hands push down on the beat
tips: Watch the hands of someone whose dancing you like, then borrow one gesture
mistakes: Arms hanging straight down, which reads as 'not dancing'
Arms flying wide on a crowded floor
why: Most people feel awkward because of their arms, not their feet. A default arm position takes that worry away.

name: Dancing in a crowd
summary: Keep your moves inside your own footprint, and go bigger only when there's space.
steps: Before you start, notice how much room you have around you
On a packed floor, keep feet under your hips and elbows in
Save spins, kicks and wide arms for when a gap opens
If you bump someone, a quick smile or hand on the heart is all it takes
tips: Face the DJ or the speakers when it's packed: everyone moves the same way and nobody collides
mistakes: Practising a big new move in the middle of a packed floor
why: Being easy to dance next to is the fastest way to feel welcome on any floor.

name: Body roll
summary: A wave that starts in the chest and rolls down through the belly and hips into the knees. Slow it down for goth, speed it up for house.
steps: Feet hip-width, knees soft
Push the chest forward on 1
Let the belly follow on 2 as the chest settles back
Push the hips forward on 3
Bend the knees on 4, then reset and start again from the chest
tips: Practise side-on to a mirror or a dark window
Start with one roll every bar; once it flows, try one every two beats
mistakes: Moving everything at once, which turns the roll into a lean
Pushing the head forward like a pigeon: the head rides along, it doesn't lead
why: It fits almost any genre and makes a plain bounce look like dancing. It's also the root of a lot of house, vogue and goth arm and torso work.

name: Quarter turns
counts: A step-touch, then turn a quarter on the last touch
summary: Keep the step-touch going and turn a quarter of the way round every four beats, so you face a new part of the room.
steps: Do one full step-touch: right, touch, left, touch
On the last touch, turn a quarter to your left on the balls of your feet
Carry on facing the new way
Four quarter turns bring you back to where you started
tips: Turn on the start of a phrase (every 8 or 16 beats) once four beats feels easy
Spot a light or a speaker for each wall so you don't get dizzy
mistakes: Stopping the feet to turn: the touch is the turn
Turning into someone's space. Glance before you go
why: Facing one way all night is what makes people look stuck. Small turns let you dance with the whole floor, and they're the base of every spin later on.

name: Half and double time
counts: Bounce every 2 beats · every beat · twice a beat
summary: Keep the same beat but change how often you move to it: half as often for a slow, heavy feel, twice as often to lift the energy.
steps: Knee bounce on every beat to find the tempo
Now bounce only on 1 and 3: that's half time
Back to every beat
Now bounce on every beat and every "and": that's double time
Switch between them when the music changes
tips: Half time suits breakdowns and goth tracks; double time suits build-ups and fast hi-hats
Try it on the practice beat with Half time switched on and off
mistakes: Speeding the bounce up instead of fitting twice as many into the same beat
Making double time bigger. Make it smaller, or it gets tiring fast
why: Matching the music's energy, not just its tempo, is the step from moving in time to actually dancing to the track.

name: Half-time drift
counts: Step on 1, hold 2 · step on 3, hold 4
summary: Slow, gliding steps on every other beat, as if you were walking through water.
steps: Step slowly to the side, or a little forward, on 1
Let the other foot follow and settle on 2, no rush
Step the other way on 3, settle on 4
Keep the upper body tall and let the head turn slowly with the steps
tips: Roll through the whole foot when you step, heel to toe or toe to heel
Close your eyes for a few bars to stop yourself rushing
mistakes: Stepping on every beat, which turns it into a march
why: Dancing in half time is what makes goth dancing look effortless, even at a club tempo.

name: Cobweb hands
summary: Hands slowly push and part the air in front of you, as if you were clearing away cobwebs.
steps: Bring both hands up in front of your face, palms out
Over two beats, sweep one hand slowly out and down to the side
Over the next two, the other hand follows on its own path
Let the wrists lead and the fingers trail behind
tips: Change levels: high above the head, then low by the hips
Your eyes can follow one hand, which adds a lot of drama for free
mistakes: Moving both arms the same way at the same time, which looks mechanical

name: Slow turn
summary: A small, unhurried turn on the spot in tiny steps, with the arms trailing.
steps: Turn your head and shoulders a little first to start the turn
Take tiny steps on the spot in that direction, one every two beats
Finish facing the front after 8 beats
Let one arm float out behind you as you turn
tips: Pick a spot on the wall and find it again at the end, so you don't get dizzy
Turn the other way next time, so both sides get practice
mistakes: Spinning on one foot, which is fast and needs much more space

name: Pushing the fog
counts: Push over 2 beats · draw back over 2
summary: The classic: both palms push slowly forward through thick fog, then draw back in. If you only learn one goth arm move, this is it.
steps: Hands at chest height, palms facing out, elbows bent
Over two beats, push both palms slowly forward as if the air were heavy
Over the next two, draw them back in toward your chest
Step with the half-time drift underneath, pushing as you step
tips: Push to the side, up, or down toward the floor to vary it
Lean the chest a little into the push so it comes from the body, not just the arms
mistakes: Pushing fast: the fog is thick, so it takes the full two beats
why: It's the move people mean when they joke about goth dancing, and that's exactly why it works: everyone on the floor recognises it.

name: Catching bats
summary: One hand reaches up and snatches something out of the air, then the other. Slow reach, quick catch.
steps: Reach one hand slowly up and out, fingers open
Close the hand sharply on the snare, as if you caught something
Bring the fist down toward your chest
The other hand reaches up for the next one
tips: The contrast is the trick: drift slowly, catch fast
Follow the hand with your eyes as it reaches
mistakes: Grabbing on every beat, which turns it into a punch

name: Picking up pennies
summary: Bend low and scoop something up off the floor, then rise and let it go above your head.
steps: Bend the knees and let one hand sink toward the floor over two beats
Scoop the hand as if picking something up
Rise over the next two beats, lifting the hand up past your face
Open the hand and let it go at the top, then switch sides
tips: Bend through the knees, not the back
Great for a breakdown or a quiet intro, when the floor slows down
mistakes: Bending over with straight legs, which is hard on the back and looks like you dropped your keys

name: Wrist twirls
counts: One circle per beat, or per two
summary: Hands circle slowly at the wrists with the fingers trailing, up by your face or above your head.
steps: Raise your hands to face height or higher, elbows soft
Circle each hand at the wrist, the fingers following a moment later
Let the hands turn in opposite directions, or one after the other
Slowly travel the hands up, out and down while they keep turning
tips: Soft, spread fingers look better than a flat hand
Add this to the half-time drift or the hip sway for a full look
mistakes: Turning the whole forearm instead of the wrist
why: A lot of the classic post-punk front-women danced with their hands. Wrist twirls are the easiest way into that look.

name: Hip sway
summary: The weight-shift sway, slowed to half time, with the hips drawing a lazy figure of eight.
steps: Start the weight-shift sway, one shift every two beats
As your weight arrives on one side, let the hip push out and round to the back
Carry it through the middle and round on the other side
Let the shoulders roll gently the opposite way to the hips
tips: Darkwave and coldwave tracks with a heavy bass line are perfect for this
Keep the feet still and let the movement live above the knees
mistakes: Rocking the hips straight side to side, which loses the curve

name: Wandering circle
summary: Drift slowly round a small circle or figure of eight on your own patch of floor, as goth floors traditionally do.
steps: Pick a patch of floor about a stride across
Drift-step round it, one step every two beats
Every few bars, change direction or cut across the middle
Keep the arms busy with fog pushes or wrist twirls as you go
tips: Watch the floor first: if people are all wandering, there's room; if they're all facing the DJ, stay put
mistakes: Wandering out of your patch into someone else's
why: Goth floors often move as slow, wandering circles rather than facing the stage. Joining that flow is how you look like you belong.

name: Deathrock stomp
summary: For the faster, punkier tracks: two heavy steps forward, two back, knees lifting, in full time.
steps: Step forward with a heavy, flat foot on 1, the other on 2
Step back on 3 and 4
Lift the knees a little and let the heels land hard
Shoulders hunched slightly forward, arms loose or pumping
tips: Switch the beat counter to full time for this one
Drop back into the half-time drift when the track eases off
mistakes: Big strides: a step the length of your foot is plenty
why: Not every goth track is slow. Deathrock and the faster post-punk need something with more punch, and this is the usual answer.

name: Cape swirl
summary: A slow half turn with the arms sweeping out and round, as if swirling a long cape behind you.
steps: Cross one arm in front of your chest
Start the slow turn, and as you do, sweep that arm out wide
Let the other arm follow, both trailing behind the turn
Finish facing away, then swirl back the other way
tips: Long sleeves, coats and skirts make this look fantastic
Only on a floor with room: check behind you first
mistakes: Swinging the arms fast, which hits people instead of looking dramatic

name: Stomp march
counts: Right on 1 · left on 2 · right on 3 · left on 4
summary: March on the spot, putting each foot down flat and heavy, right on the kick drum.
steps: Lift your right knee a little and stamp the foot down flat on 1
Same with the left on 2
Keep the knees soft as you land, so the stomp goes into the floor and not your joints
Lean the upper body slightly forward
tips: Hit harder on 1 than on the other beats
Wear boots you can stomp in. Barefoot practice at home is fine, just softer
mistakes: Landing with a straight leg, which jars the knees

name: EBM two-step
summary: One foot steps forward and back on the spot while the arms pump, switching feet every few bars.
steps: Step your right foot forward and put weight on it (1)
Step it back to where it started (2)
Repeat on 3 and 4
Pump the opposite arm forward and back with the foot, fists loose
After two or four bars, switch to the left foot
tips: Lean into the forward step a little, as if pushing through a crowd
Add a small heel stomp on the back step
mistakes: Taking big steps: this move lives in a small square on the floor
why: It's the move you see on almost every EBM floor. Once you have it, you can fit in anywhere industrial is playing.

name: Punch and pull
counts: Punch on 1 and 3, pull on 2 and 4
summary: Alternate fists punch down or forward on the beat and pull back, like working a machine.
steps: Fists up at chest height, elbows bent
Drive the right fist down and forward on 1
Pull it back sharply on 2
Left fist on 3, back on 4, while the feet keep the stomp march going
tips: Keep the punches short and sharp: stopping the movement is what makes it look hard
Try punching straight up on the big drops
mistakes: Straightening the arm all the way, which looks floppy and can hurt someone nearby

name: Hammer fists
counts: Hammer on 1 and 3 · lift on 2 and 4
summary: Both fists rise together and slam down to chest height on the big beats, while the feet keep marching.
steps: Keep the stomp march going
Lift both fists up beside your head on 2
Bring them down together, hard, to chest height on 3
Lift on 4, hammer on 1, and keep going
tips: Stop the fists dead at chest height: the stop is what makes it hit
Save it for the heaviest part of the track and march with plain arms the rest of the time
mistakes: Swinging the fists all the way down to the hips, which loses the punch and the beat

name: Side stomp
counts: 1 out · 2 stomp · 3 in · 4 stomp, then the other side
summary: A heavy step-touch: step out wide, stomp the other foot beside it, come back, stomp again. Then go the other way.
steps: Step your right foot out wide on 1, knees bent
Stomp the left foot down beside it on 2
Step the right foot back in on 3
Stomp it on 4, then do the same to the left
tips: Drop your weight into the bent knees on every stomp
Let the shoulders lean a little toward the stepping foot
mistakes: Standing up tall between stomps: stay low the whole time

name: Kick and stomp
summary: Kick one foot forward on the beat, stomp it down beside the other on the next, then switch feet.
steps: Kick your right foot forward at shin height on 1
Stomp it down flat beside your left on 2
Kick the left foot forward on 3
Stomp it down on 4
tips: Keep the kicks low and short. Height doesn't matter, timing does
Pump the opposite arm with each kick, like the EBM two-step
mistakes: Leaning back to kick higher, which throws you off balance
Kicking out into the crowd: kick into the space you already have

name: Stomp combo
counts: 4 beats of each, then round again
summary: Chain the stomp march, the EBM two-step, kick and stomp, and punch and pull into one loop that fills a whole phrase.
steps: Stomp march for 4 beats
Go straight into the EBM two-step for 4
Kick and stomp for 4
Punch and pull for 4, then back to the march
tips: Change move when the music changes; most EBM tracks shift every 8 or 16 beats
Once it flows, stay on each move for 8 beats instead of 4
mistakes: Pausing between moves. The feet never stop: every switch lands on a beat

name: Cyber stomp
summary: A step-touch built from stomps, side to side, with the arms swinging the way you travel. Everything else in cyber sits on it.
steps: Step your right foot out to the side on 1
Stomp the left foot down next to it on 2
Step the left foot out to the left on 3
Stomp the right foot next to it on 4
Swing both arms low toward the side you're stepping to
tips: At 145 BPM it's quick: start it at 120 on the practice beat
Stay on the balls of your feet so you can keep it up for a whole track
mistakes: Stomping flat-footed at full speed, which tires the legs in a minute

name: Arm roll and punch
counts: Roll for 3 beats · punch up on 4
summary: The forearms roll round each other in front of the chest, once per beat, then one fist punches up.
steps: Fists in front of your chest, one above the other
Roll them round each other, like winding wool, once per beat
On 4, punch one fist straight up
Bring it back in and start rolling again
tips: Roll forward for a bar, then backward for a bar
Swap the punching hand every time
mistakes: Rolling so fast you lose the beat. One turn per beat is plenty

name: Windmill arms
summary: Straight arms sweep in big circles at your sides, one following the other, over a stomp march.
steps: March or stomp in place
Swing the right arm up, out and down in a big circle over two beats
Start the left arm half a circle behind it
Keep the circles at your sides, not in front of you
tips: This is the move that looks amazing with glowing falls or UV gloves
Shrink the circles to elbow height on a busy floor
mistakes: Doing it in a crowd without checking your space first. Look left and right before the first swing
why: Cyber dancing is made to be seen from across the room. Big, clean shapes at a steady speed read much better than lots of small moves.

name: Side kick stomp
summary: Kick one foot out to the side on the beat, stomp it back in on the next, then the other foot. The arms punch down the opposite way.
steps: Kick your right foot out to the side at knee height on 1
Stomp it back in next to the left on 2
Kick the left foot out on 3
Stomp it in on 4
Punch both fists down toward the opposite side as you kick
tips: Lean away from the kick a little to stay balanced
Try two kicks on the same foot (kick, stomp, kick, stomp) before switching
mistakes: Kicking higher than you can land on time

name: Stomp turn
summary: Stomp march on the spot while turning slowly round, an eighth of a turn with every stomp.
steps: Start the stomp march, fists at chest height
With each stomp, point your toes a little further to the left
After eight stomps you're facing the front again
Next time, turn the other way
tips: Keep your eyes level and pick out each wall as you pass it
Pump the fists in time with the feet
mistakes: Turning in one big hop: the turn is spread over all eight stomps

name: Cyber combo
counts: 4 beats of each, then round again
summary: Cyber stomp, windmill arms, side kick stomp and the arm roll, back to back without dropping the beat.
steps: Cyber stomp for 4 beats
Windmill arms for 4, feet still stomping
Side kick stomp for 4
Arm roll and punch for 4, then back to the cyber stomp
tips: Learn it at 120 BPM, then nudge the tempo up a few beats at a time
Hit the punch on the drop and it looks planned even if nothing else was
mistakes: Letting the arms get smaller and smaller as you tire. Fewer, bigger moves beat lots of small ones

name: Swivel in place
counts: Out on the beat · in on 'and'
summary: Both feet twist together on the balls of the feet, heels out and in, without going anywhere. The first piece of every shuffle.
steps: Feet together, weight on the balls of your feet, knees soft
On the beat, twist both heels out so your toes point in
On the 'and', twist them back so your feet are straight
After eight, swap: toes out on the beat, back in on the 'and'
tips: Start barefoot or in socks on a smooth floor
Keep the knee bounce going underneath: the twist rides on top of it
mistakes: Lifting the feet. They stay on the floor and pivot
Sitting back on your heels, which jams the twist
why: Once the swivel happens without thinking, the heel-toe sidestep and the T-step are just this, pointed somewhere.

name: Knee lift
counts: Lift on 'and' · down on the beat
summary: March on the spot, but put the foot down on the beat and lift on the 'and'. This is the timing of the running man.
steps: Stand tall, weight on the balls of your feet
On the 'and', lift your right knee to about hip height
On the beat, put it down
Lift the left on the next 'and', down on the beat, and keep alternating
tips: Count out loud: 'and one, and two'. The lift always comes first
Swing the opposite arm forward, like walking
mistakes: Landing on the 'and', which puts the whole move off the beat

name: Slide back
counts: Slide on the beat · lift on 'and'
summary: Half a running man: one knee lifts and lands in front while the standing foot slides back. Learn one side, then the other.
steps: Stand on your left foot with the right knee lifted
On the beat, put the right foot down in front and slide the left foot back at the same moment
On the 'and', lift the right knee again and drag the left foot back in under you
Do eight, then swap legs
tips: Socks on a wooden or tiled floor make the slide easy to feel
The slide is short, about a foot's length
mistakes: Stepping back instead of sliding: the back foot never leaves the floor
Leaning back as the foot slides; keep the chest a little forward
why: The running man is this slide, swapping legs every beat. Get each side smooth alone and the full move is just alternating them.

name: Side kick
counts: Kick on the beat · in on 'and'
summary: A small, low kick out to the side and back, with a bounce in the standing knee. No hop yet.
steps: Weight on your left foot, right foot light
On the beat, flick the right foot out to the side, low
On the 'and', bring it back in next to the left
Four kicks, then swap and kick with the left
tips: Point the kicking foot's toes forward, not up
Hands loose at waist height help you balance
mistakes: Kicking high, which tips you over and is slow to recover
why: The kick is what you add to the swivel to make the T-step, and to a hop to make the Spongebob.

name: One-foot swivel
counts: Toes on the beat · heel on 'and'
summary: Stand on one foot and walk it sideways by twisting toes, then heel. Add the side kick and you're doing the T-step.
steps: Rest a hand on a wall or chair. Stand on your left foot, right knee lifted
On the beat, twist the left toes out to the left
On the 'and', twist the left heel out to the left: you've moved a little
Four swivels left, then stand on the right and swivel back
tips: Let go of the wall once it's steady
When it feels easy, flick the lifted foot out on each beat: that's the T-step
mistakes: Hopping the foot along instead of pivoting it
Dropping the lifted knee to catch your balance

name: Charleston walk-through
counts: 1 tap forward · 2 step · 3 tap back · 4 step
summary: The shuffle Charleston at walking pace: taps instead of kicks, and no hops, so you can learn the pattern first.
steps: Step forward on your right foot and tap the left toes out in front (1)
Bring the left foot down next to the right (2)
Step back on the left and tap the right toes behind you (3)
Bring the right foot back in (4), and repeat
tips: Say it as you go: 'tap, step, tap, step'
Once it's automatic, turn the taps into small kicks and add a bounce
mistakes: Moving forward a little each time. Forward and back cancel out, so you stay in one spot

name: First shuffle combo
summary: Your first link: eight beats of running man straight into eight of the Charleston, and back round.
steps: Running man for 8 beats
On beat 8, land the right foot in front and kick the left forward: that's the first Charleston kick
Charleston twice through, 8 beats
Back into the running man on the next 1
tips: Slow the beat to 100 BPM for the first few rounds
Once the switch is smooth, try the full Shuffle combo on the Rave tab
mistakes: Pausing at the switch: the bounce never stops, even if the feet hesitate
why: Shuffling is mostly linking. Getting from one move to the next on the 1 is what makes it look like dancing, not drills.

name: Rave bounce
summary: A light, springy bounce through the balls of the feet, with the chest and shoulders loose.
steps: Weight on the balls of your feet, heels just off the floor
Bounce through the ankles on each beat, knees soft
Let the chest pop forward a little with each bounce
Shoulders loose, hands relaxed at waist height
tips: Keep it small, and it'll last all night
Swap to the knee bounce now and then to rest your calves
mistakes: Jumping off the floor on every beat, which tires you out in one track
why: Rave floors run for hours. A low-effort bounce is what lets you dance from the first track to the last.

name: Running man
counts: Lift on 'and', slide on the beat
summary: Run on the spot: one knee lifts while the standing foot slides back, then they swap.
steps: Stand on your left foot and lift the right knee
On the beat, put the right foot down in front while the left foot slides back
Lift the left knee on the 'and', bringing the foot through
Put it down in front while the right foot slides back, and repeat
tips: Practise in socks on a smooth floor so the slide is easy
Learn it slowly at 100 BPM, then raise the tempo
mistakes: Hopping instead of sliding
Leaning back: keep the chest a little forward

name: T-step
summary: The standing foot swivels heel-toe to travel sideways while the other leg kicks out.
steps: Stand on your left foot with the right knee lifted
Swivel the left foot: toes out, then heel out, moving you to the left
At the same time, kick the right foot out to the side on each swivel
After four swivels, switch legs and travel the other way
tips: Learn the swivel alone first, holding on to a chair
Smooth floors and trainers help; grippy boots make it hard
mistakes: Travelling too far on a busy floor. Two swivels and back is plenty

name: Arm wave
summary: A ripple that travels from one hand, through the shoulders, to the other hand.
steps: Arms out to the sides at shoulder height
Lift the left wrist, then elbow, then shoulder, one after the other
Pass it across: right shoulder, right elbow, right wrist
Each joint drops as the next one rises
tips: Practise one joint at a time in front of a mirror
Bring it out on the breakdown, when everyone slows down
mistakes: Moving the whole arm at once, so it never ripples

name: Heel-toe sidestep
summary: Both feet swivel together, heels then toes, so you glide sideways without lifting your feet. The base of most shuffle moves.
steps: Feet together, weight on the balls of the feet
Swivel both heels out to the right (1)
Swivel both toes out to the right (2)
Keep going: you travel right. Reverse to come back
tips: Learn it barefoot or in socks first
Two or four swivels each way is enough on a busy floor
mistakes: Lifting the feet instead of sliding them
why: The swivel is the engine of shuffle. Once it's comfortable, the T-step and most combos fall into place.

name: Shuffle Charleston
counts: 1 kick forward · 2 step · 3 kick back · 4 step
summary: A small kick forward and a tap back, with a hop on the standing foot each time, borrowed from the old Charleston.
steps: Step forward on your right foot and kick the left foot forward (1)
Bring the left foot down next to the right (2)
Step back on the left and tap the right foot back behind you (3)
Bring it back in (4), with a small hop on the standing foot each time
tips: Turn the knees in on the kick for the classic look
Start at 110 BPM and speed up once it's smooth
mistakes: Kicking high: keep it low and quick

name: Spongebob
counts: Kick out on the beat · in on 'and'
summary: Hop on one foot while the other kicks out to the side, then cross back in. Swap feet every few beats.
steps: Stand on your left foot, right knee slightly lifted
Hop on the left as the right foot kicks out to the right side (1)
Bring the right foot back in front of the left on the 'and'
After a few kicks, switch: stand on the right, kick with the left
tips: Keep the hop tiny: it's a bounce, not a jump
Swing the arms in the opposite direction to the kick
mistakes: Kicking forward instead of to the side

name: Shuffle combo
summary: Chain the running man, the T-step and the Charleston into one flowing loop.
steps: Running man for 8 beats
On the last one, keep the knee up and go straight into the T-step for 8
T-step back the other way for 8
Drop into the Charleston for 8, then back to the running man
tips: Switch on the start of a phrase, often when a new sound comes in
Smooth links matter more than speed
mistakes: Stopping between moves: keep the bounce going through every switch

name: Fist pump
counts: Pump on every beat · swap hands every 8
summary: One fist punches up toward the ceiling on each beat while the other rests at your chest. The classic big-room move.
steps: Keep the rave bounce going
Bring your right fist up beside your shoulder
Punch it up on each beat and pull it back on the "and"
After eight, swap hands
tips: Go double time on a build-up, then both fists up on the drop
Keep the elbow a little bent at the top
mistakes: Punching forward instead of up, which takes up the space of the person in front

name: Liquid hands
summary: The hands flow around each other in front of the body without ever stopping, as if moving through water. Lovely in a trance breakdown.
steps: Hands at chest height, palms facing each other, elbows soft
Let the left hand rise while the right one sinks, as if passing a ball between them
Roll the wrists as they pass, so the palms keep facing the moving hand
Swap: right rises, left sinks, and keep it going
tips: Move in slow motion compared to the beat; the bounce keeps time for you
Watch the hands. Wherever you look, people look too
mistakes: Stopping at the top or bottom: liquid never stops, it changes direction smoothly
Stiff fingers. Let them trail behind the wrist
why: Liquid grew up with glowsticks and gloving at raves. It's the arm style to fall back on when the music goes soft and dreamy and the feet calm down.

name: The jack
summary: The heartbeat of house: the chest pulses forward on every beat and back on the "and", with the knees soft underneath.
steps: Feet hip-width, knees soft, arms loose
On the beat, push the chest forward and let the knees dip
On the "and", let the chest come back
Keep it going under every other house step
tips: Think of being pushed from behind on each kick drum
Try it side to side, or rolling in a circle, once forward and back is easy
mistakes: Nodding the head instead of moving the chest
Bending from the waist: the movement lives between the shoulder blades
why: Jacking came out of Chicago house clubs. Once it's there, any footwork on top of it looks like house dancing.

name: House stomp
counts: And tap · 1 stomp · and tap · 2 stomp
summary: Tap one foot in next to the other on the "and", then put it down flat out to the side on the beat. Then the other foot.
steps: Jack gently to find the groove
On the "and", tap the left toes in next to the right foot
On 1, put the left foot down flat out to the side
Tap the right foot in on the "and", put it down out to the side on 2
tips: Keep the jack going in the chest the whole time
Make the taps light and the stomps heavy
mistakes: Hopping: the weight moves, the body stays level

name: Skate
counts: 1 glide right · 2 draw in · 3 glide left · 4 draw in
summary: Push off one foot and glide the other out to the side, as if ice skating, then draw the trailing foot in.
steps: Bend the knees a little more than usual
Push off the left foot and glide the right foot out to the side on 1
Draw the left foot in along the floor on 2
Glide out to the left on 3, draw the right in on 4
Let the arms swing gently with the glide
tips: Works best in smooth-soled shoes
Make it smaller and quicker on a crowded floor
mistakes: Lifting the feet: they slide along the floor

name: Pas de bourrée
summary: Three quick steps over a beat and a half: cross behind, step to the side, step in place. Borrowed from ballet, beloved of house dancers.
steps: Step the right foot behind the left on 1
Step the left foot out to the side on the "and"
Step the right foot down in place on 2
Then mirror it: left behind on 3, right to the side on the "and", left in place on 4
tips: Say "back, side, front" out loud until your feet know it
Stay on the balls of your feet so the steps can be quick and small
mistakes: Big steps: the whole thing fits inside a small square

name: Loose legs
counts: Flick on the "and" · land on the beat
summary: A relaxed leg flicks out to the side and drops back under you, swapping feet each beat, as if the legs were made of rope.
steps: Jack lightly to find the groove
On the "and", flick the right foot out to the side, knee loose
Land it back under you on the beat
Flick the left on the next "and", land it on the beat
tips: The flick comes from the hip; the knee and ankle just follow
Lean the upper body a little away from the flick
mistakes: Kicking with a straight, stiff leg. Loose legs is a flick, not a kick

name: Crossroads
summary: One foot crosses over the other, then steps back out wide. Then the other foot. Simple, and it opens the door to a lot of house footwork.
steps: Cross your right foot over in front of the left on 1
Step it back out to the right on 2
Cross the left over in front of the right on 3
Step it back out to the left on 4
tips: Let the hips turn a little with each cross
Once it's easy, cross behind instead of in front every other time
mistakes: Crossing so far you trip over your own foot. A small cross is enough

name: House combo
counts: 4 beats of each, then round again
summary: House stomp, pas de bourrée, loose legs and crossroads linked into one 16-beat phrase of footwork.
steps: House stomp for 4 beats
Pas de bourrée right and left for 4
Loose legs for 4
Crossroads for 4, then back to the stomp
tips: Keep the jack going in the chest through every change
Switch the order once it's easy, so it never looks rehearsed
mistakes: Watching your feet. Look up: house is danced to the room

name: Catwalk
summary: Walk in place as if on a runway: each foot crosses onto a line in front of you and the hips swing out over it.
steps: Stand tall, chin up, shoulders back and down
Step the right foot onto an imaginary line in front of you on 1
Let the right hip swing out as the weight arrives
Step the left foot onto the line on 2, left hip out
Let the arms swing long and loose with the hips
tips: Attitude does half the work. Pick a point at eye level and own it
Walk forward for 4 and back for 4 if there's room
mistakes: Looking at your feet
Swinging the shoulders as much as the hips: the top stays calm

name: Strike a pose
summary: Catwalk for seven beats, then freeze into a sharp pose on the eighth, right on the accent in the music.
steps: Catwalk for seven beats
On 8, stop dead with the weight on one leg and the other hip popped
One hand on the hip, the other framing the face, chin turned
Hold it for a beat, then walk out of it
tips: Listen for the crash or the "ha" sound in ballroom tracks and pose on it
Have three poses ready so you never have to think of one
mistakes: Drifting into the pose. It should hit like a photo flash

name: Hand performance
summary: The hands tell the story: frame the face, sweep out, trace down the body and flick out at the wrists.
steps: Frame your face with both hands on 1
Sweep one hand out to the side, palm flat, on 3
Trace both hands down the front of the body on 5
Flick both wrists out wide on 7, then start again
tips: Keep the fingers long and together; the wrists do the flicking
Look at your hands as they move. The eyes sell it
mistakes: Rushing from one shape to the next. Arrive, hold, then move
why: Hands are the easiest way into vogue, and you can do them anywhere: on a crowded floor, in a queue, sitting down.

name: Arm control
counts: Hit a new shape on every beat
summary: Old-way vogue: the arms make sharp boxes and straight lines around the head and body, snapping from one to the next on the beat.
steps: Make a box above your head on 1: forearms flat, elbows out
Snap the right arm straight out to the side, left hand in front of the face, on 2
Drop both hands to the hips, elbows out, on 3
Left arm straight out, right hand in front of the face, on 4
tips: Keep every angle a right angle; the precision is the look
Move only the arms at first. Add a hip pop on each hit later
mistakes: Soft, curvy arms: this one is all lines

name: Spin and pose
summary: A quick full turn on the ball of one foot that lands straight into a pose.
steps: Step the right foot out and bend the knees on 1, arms in to the chest
Spin to the left on the ball of your left foot on 2, arms tight
Land facing the front and hit a pose on 3
Hold it on 4
tips: Spot: keep your eyes on one point and whip the head round last
Try a half turn first, landing facing the back
mistakes: Throwing the arms out during the spin, which slows it and can hit someone

name: Duckwalk
counts: A kick on every beat, low down
summary: Crouch low on the balls of your feet and kick the feet forward one at a time, bouncing on the beat. One of the five elements of vogue fem.
steps: Bend deep at the knees with your heels up and your back straight
Arms out in front for balance
Kick the right foot forward on 1 and put it back under you
Kick the left on 2, and keep a small bounce going
tips: Only go as low as your knees are happy. Half height still reads
Practise holding the crouch for 8 counts before adding the kicks
mistakes: Letting the knees fall in. Keep them over the toes
Trying dips (the drop to the floor) without a teacher and a forgiving floor. Those aren't taught here
why: Vogue comes from the Black and Latinx queer ballroom scene in New York. Duckwalk is one of its signatures, and even a few beats of it at the right moment gets a cheer.
